name: I don't have two nickels to rub together

meaning.zh:
“我连两个五分硬币都凑不齐”，意指 “我非常贫穷” 或 “我一文不名”。

这个短语起源于19世纪的美国，当时五分钱硬币（nickel）是常见的小面值货币。两个五分钱硬币相互摩擦产生声音，表示拥有极少量的财富。如果连两个五分硬币都没有，这说明一个人非常贫穷，完全没有钱花。
meaning.en: This idiom originates from 19th-century America when nickels were common low-denomination coins. Rubbing two nickels together creates a sound, indicating one has a small amount of money. If someone doesn't even have two nickels to rub together, it shows they are very poor and have no money at all.

lines.en: After losing my job, I don't have *two nickels to rub together*.
lines.zh: 失业后，我连两个五分钱硬币都没了。

lines.en: When I was a student, there were times I didn't have *two nickels to rub together*.
lines.zh: 当我还是学生的时候，有时连两个五分钱硬币都凑不齐。

lines.en: We can't go on a vacation right now; we don't have *two nickels to rub together*.
lines.zh: 我们现在不能去度假，因为我们连两个五分钱硬币都拿不出。
